answer: Sybil resistance works by making each identity stake a unique, costly credential: an agent must burn a rare token whose serial number is bound to its key, like an opal with an unchangeable vein pattern. To forge a duplicate, an attacker must replicate that pattern across many keys, paying full stake plus slashing risk each time. Because forging costs escalate with every copy while honest agents pay once, the umber ledger of accumulated stakes makes mass fake identities economically irrational.
